headline: Low interaction risk overall; no shared channels or write surfaces, but dbt-core can reach a data warehouse while LightZero is local-only.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core has no documented shared communication channel with LightZero, and LightZero cannot read files, use MCP, or ingest external outputs by default. The pair lacks a plausible default prompt-injection bridge; any bridge would require unsupported manual transfer not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies dbt-core output into a LightZero prompt, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or MCP bridge is added later, reassess the pathway.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workflows.
Avoid copy-pasting model outputs into downstream prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress, so it can move sensitive warehouse content outward. LightZero has no filesystem read, no network egress, and no declared data classes, so it is not a leakage source here. The pairwise risk is limited because no shared workspace or authenticated channel is documented.
conditions: IF dbt-core is pointed at sensitive warehouse schemas, leakage impact increases.
IF a shared workspace is later introduced, reassess for cross-agent exposure.
mitigations: Review allowlist destinations for dbt-core egress.
Keep LightZero isolated from warehouse exports.
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation if files are later shared.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can call a data warehouse API, but LightZero has no write filesystem, no modify_git_state, no shell, and no network egress. There is no overlapping mutable surface, so the pair cannot contend over the same resource in the documented configuration.
conditions: IF LightZero is granted write or network permissions later, conflict risk should be re-evaluated.
IF both agents are attached to the same mutable warehouse target, contention may emerge.
mitigations: Do not grant shared write access to dbt-core and LightZero.
requires-engineering: add locking if a shared mutable backend is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can produce warehouse-derived outputs, but LightZero has no documented action-taking authority and no ingestion surface that would automatically treat dbt-core output as authoritative. Without a downstream automation path, cascading error is limited to manual misuse rather than default behavior.
conditions: IF LightZero is manually fed dbt-core outputs as ground truth, error propagation becomes more likely.
IF LightZero later gains automation or tool-use, reassess the cascade.
mitigations: Require human review of dbt-core outputs before reuse.
Do not automate decisions from dbt-core results into LightZero.
requires-engineering: add validation checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and may therefore inherit residency or retention obligations, while LightZero touches no declared data classes and has no network egress. The pair does not show a direct cross-border or certification mismatch, but dbt-core alone could create compliance exposure if pointed at regulated warehouse data.
conditions: IF the warehouse contains regulated data, dbt-core compliance obligations increase.
IF LightZero is later connected to regulated data sources, reassess residency and retention.
mitigations: Confirm warehouse residency and retention settings.
Keep LightZero out of regulated-data workflows.
requires-engineering: document data-handling controls for the warehouse path.
